We use the quotient rule with the numerator $u(x)=\ln{\left(x \right)}$ and the denominator $v(x)=e^{x}.$ 

Differentiating $u(x)$ and $v(x),$ we have

$$
u'(x)=\frac{1}{x},\quad v'(x)=e^{x}.
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $v.$

Now, applying the quotient rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{\prime} & =\frac{u'(x)v(x)-u(x)v'(x)}{[v(x)]^2} \\ & =\frac{(\frac{1}{x})(e^{x})-(\ln{\left(x \right)})(e^{x})}{(e^{x})^2} \\ & =- \frac{\left(x \ln{\left(x \right)} - 1\right) e^{- x}}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
